feature.title: A7 attachments: content-addressed attachment metadata with a deferred, resumable, authorized binary path
feature.summary: Add attachments to KeepLab as a content-addressed, append-only, account-authorized, deferred binary path: a server-configurable D-13 limit set; a portable ObjectStorage abstraction with a filesystem development reference driver; a durable app-private local attachment model that streams the selected bytes, enforces the 25 MiB limit, computes SHA-256 and validates the real MIME signature; a separate resumable attachment transfer pipeline so a pending binary upload never blocks note usability; server-verified content addressing and MIME; account-scoped authorization for upload and download; same-account content deduplication that never bypasses quota, count or authorization; quota reservation inside an atomic persistence boundary; safe removal and conservative orphan handling; and a minimal attachment UX (attach an existing JPEG/PNG/WebP/PDF, show name/type/size/state, Retry, Remove).

purpose: This package is a TEMPORARY EXECUTION CONTRACT covering the whole M4 milestone (A7 attachments). It exists so that a later fresh session can implement the attachment foundation, the backend binary path, and the Android offline/upload/download path plus the minimal UX through the SAME unmodified Contract Guard, under an explicit and bounded write surface, with ONE final verification pass. This contract-creation task performed targeted discovery and authored the package; it does not implement M4.

The limits are SERVER_CONFIGURABLE and the backend is authoritative. Audio, video, application/octet-stream, arbitrary binary files, executables and archives are out of scope unless separately approved later. M4 implementation is authorized as one phase-gated milestone covering A7 attachments and nothing beyond.

boundary_notes.resolution: allowed_paths / forbidden_paths are project-relative to the Contract Guard's project-context source_root, exactly as the frozen P0B-CLOSE contract and the A0/A1/A2/M2/M3 contracts are. Entries may be exact files or directory prefixes.
boundary_notes.precedence: The guard tests forbidden_paths first; a path matching both lists is BLOCKED. reports/ is allowed while reports/contracts/ (which contains this package and every earlier package) is forbidden, so an executor cannot write its own contract or any historical package.
boundary_notes.unlisted_is_blocked: Any path inside the project root that matches neither list is BLOCKED (UNCLASSIFIED_FAIL_CLOSED).
boundary_notes.android_surface_is_enumerated_not_whole_: KeepLab-Relay/app/** is NOT authorized as a whole. Authorized: the data package (which already contains data/local, data/remote, data/sync, data/auth and may gain data/attachment), the DI package, the model package, the one NEW ui/attachment package, the named UI packages carrying attachment/sync-status integration points (settings, auth, navigation, trash, note, editor, home), the application and activity entry points, AndroidManifest.xml, app/src/main/res/xml/ only, app/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and app/src/test/**. Everything else under app/ — themes, shared UI widgets, the remaining resource directories, androidTest, benchmark, schemas, proguard rules — is BLOCKED.
boundary_notes.android_surface_rationale: Attachments genuinely need: a local attachment entity/DAO plus a schema bump (data/local), an import/storage component and a transfer component (data/, data/attachment), remote API calls and models for the upload session and download (data/remote), a durable attachment transfer pipeline (data/sync or data/attachment), DI wiring, one new ui/attachment package for the minimal attachment surface, and small integration points in the editor (attach/show/remove/state) and settings (retry/status). A whole-app authorization is therefore not required and is not granted.
boundary_notes.new_ui_attachment_package: KeepLab-Relay/app/src/main/java/com/keeplab/app/ui/attachment/ is newly authorized for M4: the minimal attachment surface. Creating it does not authorize any other new ui/ package.
boundary_notes.android_res_xml_carve_out: KeepLab-Relay/app/src/main/res/xml/ is authorized narrowly so that a specific FileProvider configuration could be added IF genuinely required (for example if an attachment must be handed to a system viewer). The existing res subdirectories (drawable, mipmap-anydpi, mipmap-anydpi-v26, values, values-night) are forbidden and must stay byte-identical, and any new resource directory is UNCLASSIFIED and therefore blocked. The expected outcome is that no resource change is needed at all: OpenDocument/SAF hands the app a readable content URI and importing the bytes into app-private storage needs no FileProvider and no manifest change.
boundary_notes.ui_conflict_package_read_only: KeepLab-Relay/app/src/main/java/com/keeplab/app/ui/conflict/ is M3's surface and is FORBIDDEN in M4: an attachment change must not edit the conflict-resolution surface.
boundary_notes.root_gradle_blocked: settings.gradle.kts, build.gradle.kts, gradle.properties, gradle/wrapper/** and gradlew are forbidden. Only app/build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml may change, and only if targeted discovery proves a dependency change is actually required, without removing or gratuitously bumping unrelated entries. ROOT_GRADLE_CHANGE: NO. A needed root Gradle change is a STOP with M4_ROOT_GRADLE_CHANGE_REQUIRED.
boundary_notes.expected_gradle_change: NO new dependency is expected: SHA-256 is java.security.MessageDigest, magic-byte MIME validation is a byte comparison, the system picker is androidx.activity (activity-compose 1.13.0, already pinned) and the server needs only ktor-server-core and java.security. The two Gradle files remain conditionally authorized so that a genuinely required addition is not a contract breach by itself; any addition must be recorded in the M4 report and must not change the root Gradle surface.
boundary_notes.backend_surface_is_whole_directory: The whole KeepLab-Relay/backend/ prefix is authorized, so ordinary compile fixes, added source files, backend-local Gradle files, resources, new Flyway migrations after V3 and backend tests never require another contract.
boundary_notes.backend_env: backend/.env.example is inside the backend prefix and may be updated with placeholders/defaults. A real backend/.env must never be created and no real credential may be written or committed anywhere.
boundary_notes.reports_contracts_read_only: reports/contracts/ is forbidden while reports/ is allowed, so this package is a READ_ONLY_INPUT for the execution session: it may be read and hashed, never written.
boundary_notes.cloud_blocked: No cloud, infra, server or firebase path is authorized; the existing backend Docker assets stay untouched in content and are never executed.
boundary_notes.device_blocked: No Android device access and no adb. androidTest and benchmark source are read-only and are never executed.
boundary_notes.out_of_project: Paths outside /mnt/AndroidDev/Projects remain OUT_OF_CONTRACT_SCOPE/ALLOW as the guard is written today; this contract does not change that guard property and must never be read as authorizing writes outside the project.
boundary_notes.guard_scope_note: The frozen guard classifies WRITE targets, not tool choice: it has no path rule that blocks an `adb` binary, `./gradlew`, `docker compose` or a container run, and it cannot classify Hermes config/core paths outside the project root. The device prohibition, the cloud prohibitions and the Hermes-core prohibition are enforced by this contract's declarations and the execution prompt's stop conditions, not by the path list. Violating one is a CONTRACT_DEVIATION. This limitation is stated rather than hidden.

requirements.statement: D-13 = ATTACHMENT_LIMITS_V1 is honoured exactly (26214400 bytes per attachment, 20 attachments per note, 1073741824 logical bytes per account, allowed MIME exactly image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, application/pdf) and every limit is SERVER_CONFIGURABLE with the backend authoritative.
The server rejects a single attachment larger than 25 MiB; the size limit is enforced from server configuration, not from a client claim.
The server rejects the 21st attachment on a note; MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_NOTE = 20 is enforced server-side.
The 1 GiB logical account quota is enforced including duplicate content: the same hash attached twice counts twice, and a pending upload reservation counts while active.
Allowed MIME is exactly JPEG/PNG/WebP/PDF; audio/*, video/*, application/octet-stream, arbitrary binary files, executables and archives are not supported.

Attachment limits are configurable through environment keys (KEEPLAB_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES, MAX_PER_NOTE, ACCOUNT_QUOTA_BYTES, ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES, CHUNK_BYTES, ORPHAN_GRACE_SECONDS) with safe M4 defaults, documented in backend/.env.example; no real backend/.env and no secret is created or committed.

An authenticated attachment configuration endpoint (GET /v1/attachments/config) returns maxBytes, maxPerNote, accountQuotaBytes, allowedMimeTypes and preferredChunkBytes and exposes no internal storage path; the Android client may cache it while the server stays authoritative.

A portable ObjectStorage abstraction exists; production business logic depends on it and never directly on a cloud SDK or filesystem API; FilesystemObjectStorage is the development/test reference driver configured by KEEPLAB_OBJECT_STORAGE_DRIVER and KEEPLAB_OBJECT_STORAGE_ROOT.
No cloud resource is provisioned (no Tencent COS, no Tencent CVM, no load balancer, no managed PostgreSQL, no cloud credential) and none is required for M4 to pass.

Objects are content-addressed by SHA-256 with account scope plus verified hash as the identity; the server verifies the actual uploaded bytes and never trusts only the client hash, the filename or the Content-Type header; user metadata cannot influence a filesystem path (no '../', no path traversal, no absolute path).

A resumable upload-session protocol exists: initiate (POST /v1/attachments/uploads) returning uploadId/chunkBytes/acceptedOffset/deduplicated-or-uploadRequired, chunk append (PUT /v1/attachments/uploads/{uploadId} with offset + binary body), status (GET) and complete (POST .../complete).
Complete verifies total byte count, SHA-256, MIME, quota reservation and note/account authorization; a hash mismatch is rejected and never becomes an UPLOADED attachment.
Upload resumes: the accepted offset and uploadId are persisted, a resuming client is told the accepted offset, and a fully-uploaded or deduplicated object reports that no further bytes are required.

Within the same account, verified identical content may reuse the stored binary, but independent attachment metadata is still created and each logical attachment still counts against the account quota and the per-note limit; deduplication never bypasses quota, the 20-attachment limit or authorization.
The service never reveals whether another account already has an identical content hash.

Download (GET /v1/attachments/{attachmentId}/content) is authorized: the authenticated account must own or access the attachment's parent note, a cross-account download is rejected, and no public anonymous object URL exists.

Quota is reserved and checked inside one atomic persistence boundary (not check-then-race-then-insert); concurrent upload initiation cannot exceed the 1 GiB logical account quota, and a reservation is released on abort, expiry or a failed initiation before commitment.

Orphan handling is conservative and explicit: an abandoned upload becomes an orphan candidate; a binary is deletable only when no attachment metadata references it, no active upload owns it and the orphan grace has elapsed; findOrphanCandidates() and cleanupEligibleOrphans() form the service boundary and cleanup never corrupts a live note.

Removing an attachment never deletes or corrupts the note: an account-scoped uploaded attachment is removed through authenticated backend semantics and an object with no remaining references becomes ORPHAN_CANDIDATE rather than being unsafely deleted inside the same metadata mutation; a LOCAL_ONLY attachment removes its metadata and its app-private file safely.

Backend authorization derives the account from the authenticated JWT subject only; a client-supplied accountId is never authority; upload and download additionally require the authenticated account to own the parent note.

A pending, offline, failed or resuming attachment upload never blocks note use: the user can still open the note and edit title/body/checklist, label, archive, pin and Trash the note; attachment failure is attachment-local.

Android imports the selected bytes into durable app-private storage by streaming (never depending permanently on a transient external content URI), enforces the 25 MiB limit while streaming when the source size is unknown, computes SHA-256, verifies the basic MIME signature and stores safely; an import failure does not corrupt note state and never leaves a partially-created usable attachment row unless the state explicitly represents failure.

MIME validation is performed against the real bytes (JPEG FF D8 FF, the PNG signature, WebP RIFF....WEBP, PDF %PDF-) and a MIME/header mismatch is a VALIDATION_ERROR that is never uploaded; no executable-detection framework and no archive support are added.

A clean local attachment model exists with the minimum concepts (stable client attachmentId, parent noteId/noteClientUuid, nullable accountId, app-private localPath, SHA-256 contentHash, sizeBytes, mimeType, displayName, uploadState, nullable remoteObjectId, uploadedBytes resume state, nullable lastErrorCode, createdAt and a removed state if required); the user filename is never the storage identity.

A LOCAL_ONLY note may hold LOCAL_ONLY attachments that remain fully local with no account and no upload, and a LOCAL_ONLY attachment is never silently adopted into an account; while the parent note stays LOCAL_ONLY the attachment stays LOCAL_ONLY.

For an account-scoped note a new valid attachment becomes UPLOAD_PENDING and is eligible for deferred upload while the note remains immediately usable; a network failure does not roll back note data and an upload failure does not mark the note unusable.

Attachment states are a small explicit set (LOCAL_ONLY, UPLOAD_PENDING, UPLOADING, UPLOADED, DOWNLOAD_PENDING, DOWNLOADING, FAILED, REMOVED or equivalent project-style names), not dozens of states, and the state survives repository/worker reconstruction because it is persisted.

Binary transfer uses its own durable attachment transfer pipeline (`attachment_sync`), separate from the existing `note_sync` pipeline, persisting the resume offset/upload id, and never creating a parallel duplicate upload for the same attachment.

Background binary upload prefers UNMETERED where practical without making attachment correctness depend forever on Wi-Fi; a manual Retry/Upload action may transfer under CONNECTED and a user-triggered download may use CONNECTED; no FCM and no push provider is introduced.

Attachment retry is bounded on the same recorded constants as M3 with no new infinite loop: network, 429 and 5xx stay retryable, while bad MIME, oversize, quota exceeded and too many attachments are permanent and are not retried forever; AUTH_REQUIRED retains the local file, the metadata and the pending transfer.

The minimal attachment UX lets the user attach an EXISTING JPEG/PNG/WebP/PDF through the Android system document/file picker restricted to the D-13 types, shows display name, type, size and transfer state, offers Retry when failed and Remove; content is re-validated after selection because picker filtering is not security validation; camera, drawing, voice and video capture are not implemented and the note editor is not redesigned.
No broad storage permission is requested: no MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and no legacy storage permission is added for attachments.

Android download streams to a temporary app-private file, verifies SHA-256 and only then atomically replaces/finalizes the local attachment file; a failed hash validation becomes FAILED and never replaces known-good local data.

Deterministic backend tests cover the M4 backend matrix: default D-13 config, configurable override, allowed MIME, blocked MIME, magic/signature mismatch, over-25-MiB rejection, the 21st-attachment rejection, the 1 GiB quota, a pending reservation participating in quota, safe reservation release, same-account dedupe, dedupe not bypassing quota, cross-account hash/object non-exposure, upload initiate, chunk upload, resume offset, complete verifying SHA-256, hash mismatch rejection, authorized download, cross-account download rejection, remove-without-corrupting-the-note, a shared content object retained while referenced, an abandoned upload becoming an orphan candidate, and orphan cleanup never removing a referenced binary.

Deterministic Android tests cover the M4 Android matrix: allowed import, disallowed MIME rejected, oversize streaming import rejected, the app-private copy surviving source abstraction loss, SHA-256 computed, a LOCAL_ONLY attachment not uploading, an account-scoped attachment becoming UPLOAD_PENDING, the note usable while an upload is pending, the upload state surviving repository reconstruction, resume using the persisted offset/uploadId, a temporary failure retaining the local file, AUTH_REQUIRED retaining the local attachment, retry resuming, a successful upload becoming UPLOADED, download hash verification, a bad downloaded hash not replacing local data, removal leaving the parent note intact and the server config overriding a client default.
M4 is device-free: no adb, no Maestro, no UiAutomator, no instrumentation run and no APK installation; DEVICE = NOT_USED.

Verification is ONE pass: each final gate runs once, a failure fixes the failed path only and re-runs only the failed task, the already-passed side is never re-run, and PASS means STOP with no post-PASS review or audit.
M4 does not start A8 multi-device, A9 multi-account, collaboration, cloud deployment, release hardening or Google Keep work, and never touches Testapp or PowerAi.

This contract package stays READ_ONLY_INPUT, the Contract Guard and the hook wiring are never modified, Hermes core is never patched, and A0/A1/A2/M2/M3 are not reopened without new explicit failure evidence.

No secret reaches source, evidence, logs or the APK: no cloud credential, no backend .env, no attachment bytes logged, and object-storage credentials (when production exists later) belong only to backend infrastructure.

failure_rule.repeated_failure: If the same failure survives two genuine fixes: emit REPEATED_FAILURE and perform one root-cause analysis.
failure_rule.allowed_patch_surface: Only files inside allowed_paths may be edited to fix a failure. A fix that would need a root Gradle change, a forbidden Android file, an existing resource directory or a new dependency outside the backend/Android dependency surface is a STOP, not a workaround.
failure_rule.gate_rule: Do not re-run the already-passed gate side. A backend failure never justifies re-running the Android gate, and an Android failure never justifies re-running the backend gate.

overhead_rule.statement: M4 is a large milestone and implementation may naturally take time, but process overhead must not dominate.
overhead_rule.rule: After contract activation, the stale-input check and one targeted discovery pass, begin implementation immediately. If process-only work dominates implementation: PROCESS_OVERHEAD_TOO_HIGH — simplify and execute.

decisions.statement: M4 is executed as ONE milestone with ONE contract, ONE execution session and ONE final verification pass: attachment foundation -> backend binary path -> Android offline/upload/download path -> minimal UX -> verify once. Attachment metadata, upload and download are NOT split into separate contracts and no Attachment/Storage/Upload Review is created.
decisions.rationale: The human directive explicitly forbids splitting metadata/upload/download into separate contracts and forbids the reviews; they add overhead without adding a verifiable outcome.

decisions.statement: D-13 = ATTACHMENT_LIMITS_V1 is frozen from HUMAN_PROJECT_OWNER_APPROVAL, 2026-10-06 and recorded in reports/KEEPLAB-M4-HUMAN-DECISIONS.md: MAX_SINGLE_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 26214400, MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_NOTE = 20, ACCOUNT_ATTACHMENT_QUOTA_BYTES = 1073741824, ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES = image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, application/pdf, LIMIT_AUTHORITY = SERVER_CONFIGURABLE.
decisions.rationale: The human directive freezes these exact values and forbids reinterpretation; audio, video, octet-stream, arbitrary binary, executables and archives stay out of scope.

decisions.statement: Quota is logical: ACCOUNT_ATTACHMENT_QUOTA_BYTES counts the logical attachment bytes owned by the account, duplicate files do not bypass it, the same content hash may deduplicate the stored binary while both logical attachments still count, and a pending upload reservation counts while active so concurrent uploads cannot race past the quota; a reservation is released on abort, expiry or a failed initiation before commitment.
decisions.rationale: The human directive states this quota semantics explicitly; the reservation rule is what makes the atomic boundary meaningful.

decisions.statement: M4 implements a portable ObjectStorage abstraction with FilesystemObjectStorage as the development/test reference driver, configured by KEEPLAB_OBJECT_STORAGE_DRIVER and KEEPLAB_OBJECT_STORAGE_ROOT. Production business logic depends on ObjectStorage, never directly on a Tencent COS SDK, an AWS SDK or filesystem APIs. No cloud resource is provisioned and no cloud credential exists. The filesystem driver is explicitly a DEVELOPMENT_REFERENCE_DRIVER, not a claim that production Tencent COS exists; a Tencent adapter may be added later at deployment/infrastructure time without changing attachment domain logic.
decisions.rationale: D-08 selected Tencent Cloud and portable Docker as the production target, and the human directive forbids provisioning it in M4 while requiring the abstraction that keeps the domain logic vendor-free.

decisions.statement: The backend is the limit authority. Every limit is server-configurable through KEEPLAB_ATTACHMENT_* keys with the D-13 values as the safe defaults, and the Android client may only pre-validate for UX using cached server limits or the D-13 defaults. The server enforces regardless of what a client believed.
decisions.rationale: The human directive requires SERVER_CONFIGURABLE limits with the backend authoritative, and allows client-side pre-validation for UX only.

decisions.statement: Content addressing uses SHA-256 and the server verifies the ACTUAL uploaded bytes; it never trusts only the client hash, filename or Content-Type header. Object identity is account scope + verified hash (recommended key shape accounts/<accountId>/sha256/<hash>); the user filename is never the object key; user metadata can never influence a filesystem path (no '../', no traversal, no absolute path).
decisions.rationale: The human directive states each of these as mandatory, and they are the security boundary of the binary path.

decisions.statement: The upload protocol is a small resumable upload session: initiate, chunk append with an offset, status/resume, and complete. Route naming may follow the existing Ktor style. Multipart and cloud-presigned architecture must not be overbuilt, and a cloud-presigned design is explicitly not adopted.
decisions.rationale: The human directive requires resume support and forbids overbuilding multipart/presigned architecture; a session with an accepted offset is the smallest correct design.

decisions.statement: Within the same account, verified identical content may reuse the stored binary, but independent attachment metadata is still created and each logical attachment still counts against account quota and the per-note limit. Deduplication never bypasses the maximum attachment count, the quota or authorization, and the service never reveals whether another account already has an identical hash.
decisions.rationale: The human directive states both the dedupe permission and every bypass it must not enable, plus the cross-account non-disclosure requirement.

decisions.statement: Download is authenticated: the authenticated account must own or access the attachment's parent note, and no public anonymous object URL exists. On Android a download streams to a temporary app-private file, verifies SHA-256 and only then atomically replaces/finalizes the local file; a hash mismatch is FAILED and must not replace known-good local data.
decisions.rationale: The human directive states the authorization rule and the Android verification/atomic-replace rule.

decisions.statement: Quota enforcement is not check-then-race-then-insert: the backend reserves/checks quota inside one atomic persistence boundary appropriate to the current store, so concurrent upload initiation cannot exceed the 1 GiB logical account quota, and MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_NOTE = 20 is likewise server enforced.
decisions.rationale: The human directive names the race explicitly and requires an atomic boundary; the in-memory store and the JDBC store must both honour it.

decisions.statement: Removal is safe: removing an attachment never deletes or corrupts the note. An account-scoped uploaded attachment is removed through authenticated backend semantics; an object with no remaining references becomes an ORPHAN_CANDIDATE and is not unsafely deleted inside the same metadata mutation unless transactional correctness is proven. A LOCAL_ONLY attachment removes its metadata and its app-private local file safely.
decisions.rationale: The human directive states the removal rule and explicitly warns against unsafe in-mutation deletion.

decisions.statement: Orphan handling is conservative: an abandoned upload, a binary whose metadata finalize failed, a removed attachment and a deduplicated binary still referenced elsewhere are all handled; a binary is deletable only when no attachment metadata references it, no active upload owns it and the orphan grace has elapsed; cleanup never corrupts a live note. findOrphanCandidates() and cleanupEligibleOrphans() are the service boundary; a full production scheduler is NOT built in M4.
decisions.rationale: The human directive names the scenarios, the conservative rule and the sufficiency of an explicit service boundary.

decisions.statement: The local attachment model is clean and content-addressed: stable client attachmentId, parent note identity, nullable accountId for LOCAL_ONLY, app-private localPath, SHA-256 contentHash, sizeBytes, mimeType, displayName, uploadState, nullable remoteObjectId, uploadedBytes resume state, nullable lastErrorCode and createdAt. The user filename is neither the storage identity nor a path component.
decisions.rationale: The human directive specifies the minimum concepts and forbids using the filename as identity.

decisions.statement: Import is durable and streaming: the selected bytes are copied into KeepLab app-private storage, streaming the data and enforcing the 25 MiB limit (including when the source size is unknown), computing SHA-256 and verifying the basic MIME signature. The app never depends permanently on a transient external content URI. An import failure does not corrupt note state and never leaves a partially-created usable attachment row unless the state explicitly represents failure.
decisions.rationale: The human directive requires durability independent of the picker URI, streaming enforcement and a non-corrupting failure path.

decisions.statement: MIME validation is signature-based on the real bytes (JPEG FF D8 FF, the PNG signature, WebP RIFF....WEBP, PDF %PDF-); the extension alone is never trusted; a mismatch is a VALIDATION_ERROR that is not uploaded. No executable-detection framework and no archive support are added.
decisions.rationale: The human directive specifies exactly these signatures and explicitly bounds the effort.

decisions.statement: A LOCAL_ONLY note may hold LOCAL_ONLY attachments that stay fully local; a LOCAL_ONLY attachment is never silently adopted into an account and stays LOCAL_ONLY while its parent note does. The existing no-silent-adoption policy is preserved.
decisions.rationale: The human directive states this and it matches MISSION invariant 1 as already implemented by the note repository.

decisions.statement: On an account-scoped note a new valid attachment becomes UPLOAD_PENDING and is eligible for deferred upload while the note remains immediately usable; a network failure must not roll back note data and an upload failure must not mark the note unusable. The attachment states are a small explicit set (LOCAL_ONLY, UPLOAD_PENDING, UPLOADING, UPLOADED, DOWNLOAD_PENDING, DOWNLOADING, FAILED, REMOVED or project-style equivalents).
decisions.rationale: INVARIANT ATT-1 and the human directive's state list; a small explicit model prevents state sprawl.

decisions.statement: Binary transfer uses its own durable attachment transfer pipeline named `attachment_sync`, separate from the existing `note_sync` pipeline, because large binary work has different retry and network behaviour. The resume offset and upload id are persisted and no parallel duplicate upload for the same attachment may exist.
decisions.rationale: The human directive requires a separate attachment transfer queue and forbids duplicating an upload; keeping note mutation semantics untouched is the point of the separation.

decisions.statement: Network policy: background binary upload prefers UNMETERED where practical without making correctness depend forever on Wi-Fi; a manual Retry/Upload action may transfer under CONNECTED when the user explicitly asks; a user-triggered download may use CONNECTED. No FCM and no push provider is introduced.
decisions.rationale: The human directive states this policy and forbids a push provider.

decisions.statement: Attachment retry is bounded on the same principles and recorded constants as M3 (AUTO_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5, EXPONENTIAL backoff) and introduces no new infinite loop. Network, 429 and 5xx stay retryable; bad MIME, oversize, quota exceeded and too many attachments are permanent and are not retried forever. AUTH_REQUIRED retains the local file, the metadata and the pending transfer.
decisions.rationale: The human directive requires bounded retry consistent with M3, forbids an infinite loop, and requires AUTH_REQUIRED to be non-destructive.

decisions.statement: The attachment UX is the smallest useful one: attach an EXISTING JPEG/PNG/WebP/PDF through the Android system document/file picker restricted to the D-13 types, show display name, type, size and transfer state, offer Retry when failed and Remove. Content is re-validated after selection because picker filtering is not security validation. No camera/drawing/voice/video capture, no editor redesign, and an image thumbnail only if it needs no large unrelated UI or dependency work.
decisions.rationale: The human directive enumerates exactly this surface and these exclusions.

decisions.statement: No broad storage permission is requested: no MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and no legacy storage permission for attachments.
decisions.rationale: The human directive forbids both; OpenDocument/SAF needs neither.

decisions.statement: Backend authorization derives the account from the authenticated JWT subject only — a client-supplied accountId is never authority — and upload/download additionally require the authenticated account to own the parent note.
decisions.rationale: INVARIANT AUTHZ-1 and the human directive's requirement that the parent note be owned/accessible.

decisions.statement: The Android write surface is enumerated, not the whole app: data/ (including new data/attachment), model/, di/, one new ui/attachment package, the named UI integration packages, the application/activity entry points, AndroidManifest.xml, app/src/main/res/xml/ only, app/src/test/**, plus conditionally app/build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml.
decisions.rationale: Attachments genuinely need exactly those surfaces; themes, shared widgets, the other resource directories, the M3 ui/conflict package, androidTest, benchmark and schemas are provably unrelated and stay blocked.

decisions.statement: The root Android Gradle surface is unchanged; only app/build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml may change, and only if targeted discovery proves a dependency change is actually required. The expected outcome is NO dependency change (SHA-256 is java.security.MessageDigest, magic-byte validation is a byte comparison, the picker is androidx.activity already pinned, and the server needs only ktor-server-core + java.security utility APIs). ROOT_GRADLE_CHANGE: NO.
decisions.rationale: The human directive authorizes Gradle files only if targeted discovery proves a dependency change is required, and forbids broadly authorizing app/** without evidence.

decisions.statement: Room moves directly to the next clean schema version by an experimental bump with DEV_DATABASE_RESET_REQUIRED = YES for the new local attachment structures; no migration chain is authored and exportSchema stays false. The backend gains new Flyway migrations after V3 only as M4 requires, with no production compatibility chain.
decisions.rationale: Project data is disposable experimental data (CLEAN_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE > PRESERVE_TEST_DATA) and the human directive forbids building production migration complexity.

decisions.statement: M4 is device-free and cloud-free: no adb, no Maestro, no UiAutomator, no APK install, no cloud provisioning, no infrastructure installation; a live-PostgreSQL check is optional and its absence is recorded as SKIPPED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE without weakening the transactional semantics. Real picker/device UX may be validated in a later product/device milestone.
decisions.rationale: The human directive makes M4 deterministic-test-first with DEVICE = NOT_USED and forbids installing infrastructure.

decisions.statement: Verification is ONE pass with both gates run once each; a failure fixes the failed path and re-runs only the failed task; a repeated failure triggers ONE root-cause analysis; PASS means STOP with no post-PASS audit. Minor non-blocking findings are appended compactly to reports/KEEPLAB-MINOR-BACKLOG.md instead of becoming contracts.
decisions.rationale: Milestone execution: no review of review, no post-PASS audit, no re-run of a passing side, no backlog-by-count cleanup.
